findings.title: Backup code consumption is a read-modify-write race (TOCTOU)
findings.body: In the credentials authorize() handler, the backup code is validated with `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` and then consumed by re-encrypting and writing the whole array back via prisma.user.update. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both pass the indexOf check before either write lands, so a single-use code can be redeemed twice. The update should be conditional/atomic (or use a transaction/optimistic check) to guarantee one-time use, since 'each backup code can be used exactly once' is the stated security contract.

findings.title: Empty backup code submission silently does nothing on login
findings.body: The login form has `noValidate`, so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the BackupCode TextField are never enforced, and there is no zod/react-hook-form validation for `backupCode`. If a user in the 'lost access' flow submits without typing a code, `credentials.backupCode` is empty/falsy, so the authorize() branch `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` is skipped, the totpCode branch throws SecondFactorRequired, and the client just re-sets twoFactorRequired(true) — no error message is shown and nothing happens. The user gets no feedback.

findings.title: Backup code is consumed before the login is guaranteed to succeed
findings.body: The verified backup code is marked used (set to null and persisted) inside authorize(), before next-auth finishes signing the user in (JWT encoding, signIn callback, session creation). If any later step fails, the user has permanently lost a backup code without gaining access. The consumption should only happen once the sign-in is committed, or be idempotent/retryable.

findings.title: req.body.backupCode is used without type/shape validation
findings.body: The disable endpoint calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` without validating that it is a string. A client POSTing `backupCode` as an object/array/null-as-object (Next.js body parsing can produce nested JSON) causes `replaceAll is not a function`, throwing a 500. The login authorize() path in next-auth-options.ts (line 144) has the same unvalidated `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)`. Inputs should be validated (e.g. zod string) before use.

findings.title: No test actually exercises backup-code login or backup-code 2FA disable
findings.body: The PR adds backup codes as the core feature but the e2e suite only tests downloading/copying/closing the backup-code dialog. There is no test that logs in with a backup code (the primary new auth path in next-auth-options.ts), verifies a code is single-use, or disables 2FA with a backup code (the new branch in disable.ts). These are security-critical code paths; a regression would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Backup codes compared with indexOf (non-constant-time)
findings.body: Backup codes are compared using `Array.prototype.indexOf`, which uses non-constant-time string comparison on a secret. For consistency with how passwords/TOTP are verified, a timing-safe comparison is preferable, though the practical exploitability is low given network jitter. Low priority hardening.
